title: reviewmesh panel roster
description: `panel/roster.json` — the EXECUTED ROSTER of a run's blind primary reviewer panel. It carries one entry per REQUESTED seat, in requested order, including seats that halted or never started: N seats requested is N seats accounted for, or a clear failure. It is the audit-record twin of the `panel[]` block in the run projection and the ACP `_meta.reviewmesh` echo, and it is written on a halt too, so a failed run still records what the panel was.

seats.description: The panel, in AUTHORED order. There is no privileged size: a one-seat panel (the historical single reviewer) and a sixteen-seat panel are the same shape.

seatId.description: reviewer | reviewer-2 | reviewer-3 | … — seat 1 keeps the bare role name, so a panel of one records exactly what a pre-panel build recorded

status.description: completed = ran and produced a schema-valid result; budget_capped = completed, but the run-level round budget stopped further stabilization rounds (its findings are kept); halted = this seat's failure halted the RUN — there is no partial-panel success; not_started = the run halted on an earlier-indexed seat first

rounds.description: stabilization rounds this seat actually ran

findings.description: raw findings this seat reported across its rounds, BEFORE host dedup

identityTier.description: the WEAKEST identity classification observed across this seat's calls (fail closed). A finding supported only by weak-tier seats is reported but never applied.

reasonCode.description: stable machine code when the seat did not complete normally (e.g. model_identity_mismatch, adapter_exited_nonzero, reviewer_result_unparseable, panel_round_budget_exhausted)

signal.description: THIS SEAT'S own actionable classification. A panel dispatches every seat concurrently, so a halted run has usually paid for several failures with DIFFERENT causes, while the run-level halt record can name only the first by index. This is where the others are recorded.

detail.description: this seat's own one-line cause, in the same words the run-level halt uses when they are the same failure
